newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lang in A$100 mln Port Botany upgrade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lang in A$100 mln Port Botany upgrade.

text.p: The New South Wales state government said on Wednesday that Patrick Stevedores would invest A$100 million to increase the capacity of the Port Botany cargo terminal on the southern shores of Sydney.
The investment programme was linked to a 10 year extension of the Patrick lease at Port Botany to the year 2018, the government said. Patrick is a 68 pecent owned unit of Lang Corp.
Port Botany's capacity would be increased to 550,000 twenty foot equivalent units (teus) a year by 1998 compared with 330,000 teus at the moment, with a rise to 800,000 teus by 2003.

"The new investment will reinforce Sydney as Australia's premier port by securing growth in container traffic, including greater exports, into the next century," said New South Wales minister for ports, Chris Scully.

Patrick's investment would include one new Panamax container crane, the upgrading of three existing cranes, the purchase of 20 straddle carriers, the complete refurbishment of the terminal, and computerised planning and tracking of container handling operations.
